info.title: Twos API
info.description:
Read and write your Twos lists and things. A list holds things. A thing is a `todo` (a checkbox) or a plain line, and can carry a url, tags, an indent depth, and a long-form markdown note.

Authenticate with a personal API key created at https://www.twosapp.com/settings/api-keys and sent as `Authorization: Bearer twos_…`. A key only ever reaches its own owner's data, so no request takes a user id.

**Resolve ids before you use them.** Every get, update, delete, and reminder operation takes an id. Call `GET /search` to turn a name into an id, or `GET /lists` to enumerate. Ids are opaque, and a guessed one returns 404.

**Day lists come from `GET /today`.** The date-titled daily list is the center of the product. `GET /today` resolves or creates the list for today, yesterday, tomorrow, or any date. Scanning `GET /lists` for a date-titled one instead will find duplicates or nothing.

**Write in bulk.** `POST /things/bulk` creates up to 500 things in one call, and `PATCH`/`DELETE /things/bulk` change many at once. Looping the single-item routes burns the rate limit and reorders nothing faster.

**Every write is real.** There is no sandbox and no test mode. A delete removes a thing from a person's account. Confirm destructive calls with whoever asked for them.

Creates a new list. Fields you omit fall back to your account defaults (e.g. list sort). Pass `things` to create the list already filled, in one call (returns `created`/`skipped` counts alongside the list).

Requires the `write:lists` scope.

post.description:
Create a NEW list from a markdown document in one call. The title comes from `title`, or the document’s first heading (`# …`) when omitted; the rest becomes the list’s things (checkboxes → todos, `1.` → numbered, `-`/`*` → bullets, `##` → heading, `###` → subheading, indentation → nesting).

Requires the `write:lists` scope.

title.description: The new list’s name. Omit to use the markdown’s first "# Heading".

emoji.description: An emoji for the new list.

get.description:
List your things newest-first across all lists (or one list). Built for automation polling: each thing has a stable `id` for dedup, and `since` + `sort` form an incremental cursor. Filter by list, completion, type, or tag.

Requires the `read:things` scope.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Zero-based page (50 per page). Page until has_more is false to read everything.

post.description:
Creates a thing inside one of your lists. Target the list with `list_id` (from list_lists/search) or `list` (a list name, or "today"/"tomorrow"/an ISO date). Pick a `type` — `todo` (checkbox), `note`/`none` (plain), `dash`, `number`, or `bullet` — or omit it to use your default thing type. Add a `url` to make it a hyperlink, `tags` to categorize it, `list_ref` to link another list, or `created` to backdate it. To create many at once, send an `items` array to Bulk-create things instead.

Requires the `write:things` scope.

list_id.description: The id of the list to add the thing to. Omit if you pass `list`.

list.description: Alternative to list_id: a list name, or "today"/"yesterday"/"tomorrow"/an ISO date (the day list, created if needed).

text.description: The thing’s text, in markdown (**bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, [label](url)) — the same dialect reads return, so text round-trips. An unpaired marker stays literal, and a code:true thing is never parsed.

type.description: Thing type: `todo` (checkbox), `note`/`none` (plain, no marker), `dash`, `number` (numbered), or `bullet`. Omit to use your default thing type.

url.description: A hyperlink to attach to the thing.

list_ref.description: The id of another list to reference (a navigable list link). Pass a list id, not a URL.

tags.description: Tag names (with or without a leading #).

photos.description: Hosted image URLs to attach (must be http(s); max 10). The API does not host images — upload them elsewhere and pass the URLs.

created.description: ISO 8601 creation time. Use it to preserve original capture-date order when importing; omit to stamp now.

tabs.description: Indent level: 0 = top level (default); 1+ nests this thing under the preceding one. Create the parent first, then the indented children.

header.description: Make the thing a heading (H1). Mutually exclusive with `subheader`; also bolds it unless you pass `bold` explicitly.

subheader.description: Make the thing a subheading (H2). Mutually exclusive with `header`; also bolds it unless you pass `bold` explicitly.

quote.description: Style the thing as a blockquote. Mutually exclusive with `code`.

code.description: Style the thing as a code block. Mutually exclusive with `quote`.

note.description: A long-form note attached to the thing, in **markdown**. Shown behind a note icon in the app, never inline with `text`. Pass `""` to remove it. Reads return the same markdown, so a note round-trips unchanged.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per hour for this key (1000).

post.description:
Create many things in one call (one ordered insert) — use this instead of looping for imports or building a list. Send an `items` array; each item takes the same fields as Create a thing (`text`, optional `type`, `url`, `list_ref`, `tags`, `photos`, `completed`, `tabs`, `created`). Set a top-level `list_id` as the default target, or give each item its own. `skip_duplicates: true` skips items already present (by url, else text), making re-runs safe. Returns per-list counts, not the items. Max 500 per call.

Requires the `write:things` scope.

items.description: The things to create (max 500). Each item: { text, list_id?, list?, type?, url?, list_ref?, tags?, photos?, completed?, tabs?, created?, and formatting: bold?, italic?, underline?, header?, subheader?, quote?, code? }.

list_id.description: Default list for items that don’t set their own list_id.

list.description: Alternative default target: a list name, or "today"/"tomorrow"/an ISO date.

skip_duplicates.description: Skip items already in the target list (by url, else text).

patch.description:
Apply one change set to many things at once — check them all off, move them to a list, star them. Send `ids` (the thing ids) and `set` (fields to apply to each, same shape as Update a thing). A move target (`list_id` or `list` name) is resolved once. Ids you no longer own are skipped, not errors. Max 500 ids per call.

Requires the `write:things` scope.

ids.description: Ids of the things to change (max 500).

set.description: Fields to apply to every listed thing: { completed?, canceled?, favorited?, type?, tags?, tabs?, url?, list_ref?, list_id?, list?, and formatting: bold?, italic?, underline?, header?, subheader?, quote?, code? }.

patch.description:
Updates a thing. Only the fields you send change. Set `completed`/`canceled` to complete or cancel a todo, `list_id` to move it to another list, or `list_ref` to reference another list. Content edits keep the thing’s position in its list — only moving it (new `list_id`) changes its order. Completing (or canceling) a thing with a repeating reminder works like the app: a completed copy stays where it was done, the reminder advances to the next occurrence, and the thing itself comes back open on that occurrence’s day. The response then includes `repeating_reminder` with the copy’s id and the next occurrence. Completing or canceling a thing with a one-off reminder removes the reminder, and the response includes `reminder_removed: true`.

Requires the `write:things` scope.

text.description: New text for the thing, in markdown (same dialect as reads, so a read-modify-write keeps its formatting).

list_ref.description: Set a referenced list id (a navigable list link), or pass an empty string to clear it.

photos.description: Replace the attached image URLs (http(s); max 10). Pass [] to remove all photos.

tabs.description: Indent level: 0 = top level; 1+ nests under the preceding thing.

list_id.description: Move the thing to another list you own.

list.description: Alternative to list_id for a move: a list name, or "today"/"tomorrow"/an ISO date.

header.description: Make the thing a heading (H1). Mutually exclusive with `subheader`; also bolds it unless you pass `bold` explicitly.

subheader.description: Make the thing a subheading (H2). Mutually exclusive with `header`; also bolds it unless you pass `bold` explicitly.

quote.description: Style the thing as a blockquote. Mutually exclusive with `code`.

code.description: Style the thing as a code block. Mutually exclusive with `quote`.

note.description: A long-form note attached to the thing, in **markdown**. Shown behind a note icon in the app, never inline with `text`. Pass `""` to remove it. Reads return the same markdown, so a note round-trips unchanged.

put.description:
Set or replace the reminder on a thing. A thing has at most one reminder.

Requires the `write:things` scope.

at.description: When to remind — ISO 8601. Include a timezone offset or Z for an exact time (e.g. 2026-06-03T17:00:00-04:00). A naive time (no offset) is interpreted in the user’s timezone.

all_day.description: Treat it as an all-day reminder.

duration_minutes.description: How long the calendar block lasts, in minutes. 0 gives it no end time. Defaults to your "Default reminder duration" setting. Cannot be combined with end or all_day.

end.description: When the block ends — ISO 8601, an alternative to duration_minutes. Must use the same form as at: both with a timezone offset, or both without.

every.description: Repeat every N of the chosen interval, so repeat "monthly" with every 3 is every 3 months. Defaults to 1. Cannot be combined with days.

repeat_until.description: Stop repeating after this date — ISO 8601. Must be after at.

days.description: For weekly reminders, the weekdays it repeats on — names ("monday") or 0–6 (0=Sunday). Providing days makes it weekly.

alert_minutes.description: Notify this many minutes before. Defaults to your reminder settings. 0 means no advance notice.

second_alert_minutes.description: A second, independent notification this many minutes before — e.g. 1440 for a day before, alongside a 60-minute first alert. 0 means none.

color.description: Hex color. Defaults to your default reminder color.

bearerAuth.description: A Twos API key. The person you are acting for creates one at https://www.twosapp.com/settings/api-keys, where it is shown once. Ask them for it rather than guessing, and never send it to another host.

sort.description: How things are ordered in the app. Usually `chronological` (oldest first, the default), `reverse-chronological`, `alphabetical`, `reverse-alphabetical`, `created` (oldest created first), `reverse-created` (newest created first), `modified` (most recently edited first), or `reverse-modified`. Treat an unrecognized value as `chronological`.

Thing.description: A thing (a todo or a note).

list_ref.description: If this thing links to another list (a sub-list reference), that list’s id; else null.

type.description: The thing’s style. `todo` is a checkbox, `none` is a plain line. Writes also accept `note` as an alias for `none`, but a read always returns `none`, so do not expect a write of `note` to read back unchanged.

photos.description: Hosted image URLs attached to this thing.

clone_of.description: If this thing is a clone (a live linked copy), the id of the origin thing; else null.

has_clones.description: True if this thing is an original that has one or more clones.

header.description: Whole-thing heading (H1). Mutually exclusive with subheader.

subheader.description: Whole-thing subheading (H2). Mutually exclusive with header.

quote.description: Whole-thing blockquote. Mutually exclusive with code.

code.description: Whole-thing code block. Mutually exclusive with quote.

note.description: Long-form note attached to the thing, in markdown. Shown behind a note icon in the app, never inline with `text`. Empty string when there is no note.

example.note: Prefer the **barista** blend — the oat one at the corner shop.

every.description: Repeat interval, in units of `repeat`. 2 with `weekly` means every other week.

repeat_until.description: When the repeat stops. Null repeats forever. Not the same as `end`.

days.description: Weekdays it repeats on, when repeat is weekly.

end.description: When this single occurrence ends, for a reminder that occupies a span of time.

duration_minutes.description: Length of the occurrence in minutes. The same span as `end`, expressed as a duration. Writes set one or the other, never both.

alert_minutes.description: Minutes before `at` to notify. 0 or null means no advance notice.

second_alert_minutes.description: An optional second notification, also in minutes before `at`.

color.description: Hex color. Empty when the reminder has no color of its own.
